fields.name: bias_types
fields.definition: Social bias types that the study empirically identifies or explicitly reports in an LLM-based system.
fields.unit_of_extraction: One explicitly supported item for bias_types
rules: Do not convert a general ethical concern into an observed bias.
Preserve the authors' term as raw_value and optionally provide a normalized_value.
Use reported_not_observed when the paper discusses a bias without empirically demonstrating it.
Examples: gender bias; racial or ethnic bias; age bias
Preserve the original expression; normalize to a concise textual label only when defensible, otherwise use null.

evidence_status.definition: Interpretation of the extracted item: evidence_status

fields.name: se_tasks_or_contexts
fields.definition: Software Engineering task or broader socio-technical SE context in which the bias is studied.
fields.unit_of_extraction: One explicitly supported item for se_tasks_or_contexts
rules: Classify each item as technical_task or socio_technical_context.
Do not force recruitment, hiring or professional representation into a technical SDLC task.
Examples: code generation; requirements engineering; software engineer recruitment
Preserve the original expression; normalize to a concise textual label only when defensible, otherwise use null.

context_type.definition: Interpretation of the extracted item: context_type

fields.name: llm_systems
fields.definition: LLMs, assistants or generative systems evaluated as subjects of the bias analysis.
fields.unit_of_extraction: One explicitly supported item for llm_systems
rules: Distinguish subject_under_test from auxiliary_model.
A judge model is not a subject under test unless the paper evaluates its own bias.
Examples: GPT-4; GitHub Copilot; Stable Diffusion XL
Preserve the original expression; normalize to a concise textual label only when defensible, otherwise use null.

model_role.definition: Interpretation of the extracted item: model_role

fields.name: bias_sources
fields.definition: Sources or origins of bias asserted or hypothesized by the study authors.
fields.unit_of_extraction: One explicitly supported item for bias_sources
rules: Set qualifiers.epistemic_status to demonstrated, author_hypothesis or background_claim.
Do not infer a cause merely because it is plausible.
Examples: imbalanced training data; historical workforce imbalance; prompt demographic cues
Preserve the original expression; normalize to a concise textual label only when defensible, otherwise use null.

epistemic_status.definition: Interpretation of the extracted item: epistemic_status

fields.name: evaluation_methods
fields.definition: Methods, datasets and measurements used to detect or evaluate bias.
fields.unit_of_extraction: One explicitly supported item for evaluation_methods
rules: Separate the evaluation method from the study's conclusions.
Capture sample size or number of generated artifacts when explicitly reported.
Examples: counterfactual prompting; metamorphic testing; image generation and demographic classification
Preserve the original expression; normalize to a concise textual label only when defensible, otherwise use null.

method_status.definition: Interpretation of the extracted item: method_status

fields.name: reported_impacts
fields.definition: Impacts or consequences of bias explicitly reported by the study.
fields.unit_of_extraction: One explicitly supported item for reported_impacts
rules: Record whether an impact is empirically_observed, author_inference or general_background.
Examples: reinforcement of stereotypes; unequal recruitment outcomes
Preserve the original expression; normalize to a concise textual label only when defensible, otherwise use null.

evidence_status.definition: Interpretation of the extracted item: evidence_status

fields.name: manifestations
fields.definition: Specific observable form in which bias appears in model outputs or behavior.
fields.unit_of_extraction: One explicitly supported item for manifestations
rules: Describe the observable behavior, not only the broad bias category.
Examples: gendered variable names; underrepresentation in generated images
Preserve the original expression; normalize to a concise textual label only when defensible, otherwise use null.

evidence_status.definition: Interpretation of the extracted item: evidence_status

fields.name: mitigation_strategies
fields.definition: Bias mitigation strategies proposed, implemented or empirically tested by the study.
fields.unit_of_extraction: One explicitly supported item for mitigation_strategies
rules: Set qualifiers.intervention_status to proposed, implemented or empirically_tested.
An absence claim must be explicit and supported by the inspected evidence.
Examples: fairness-aware prompting; RLHF; LoRA fine-tuning
Preserve the original expression; normalize to a concise textual label only when defensible, otherwise use null.

intervention_status.definition: Interpretation of the extracted item: intervention_status
